rows.t_avg_note: The DOE file lists $63,538 for Oyster River, about 17% below the years on either side and out of line with other districts. It is not plotted.
The DOE file repeats the 2023-24 figure of $80,573 to the dollar although the teacher count changed. It is not plotted.

meta.label: Spending, revenue and cost per pupil (actual)
meta.value: NH DOE DOE-25 Annual Financial Report, District Profile sheet, Oyster River Coop (d423000.xlsx), FY2018 to FY2025: function expenditures, Total Recurring Expenditures, Total Expenditures, revenues by source and per-pupil current expenditure. FY2026 is not yet filed.

meta.label: Adopted budget
meta.value: Operating budget warrant article as printed on each March ballot (all funds). FY2017-18 to FY2023-24 checked against the budget summary tables and warrant articles in the official ORCSD annual reports (2018 to 2023 editions) at orcsd.org; FY2025-26 and FY2026-27 also on orcsd.org.

meta.label: Inflation indexes
meta.value: US Bureau of Labor Statistics. CPI-U all items, Northeast urban, not seasonally adjusted (CUUR0100SA0) and US city average (CUUR0000SA0); Employment Cost Index, total compensation, state and local government workers in educational services (CIU3016100000000I). Fiscal-year values are July to June averages of monthly CPI and of the four quarters ending September to June. October 2025 CPI was not collected, so FY 2025-26 CPI averages 11 months; FY 2026-27 uses the months and quarters available so far.

meta.label: Attendance
meta.value: NH DOE Attendance Rate by District CSVs, 2017-18 to 2021-22 (district total, all grades). Attendance by school level for 2025-26 is from the iPlatform Attendance Rate by School report (the same report is blank for 2024-25 and earlier; DOE notes data-quality problems before 2024-25). The ORCSD annual report cards give attendance by school level for later years, but the 2022-23 and 2023-24 columns are identical to each other, and 2024-25 jumps to about 98% for both the district and the state, which looks like a change in how it is measured, so those years are not plotted.

meta.label: Instruction salaries and benefits
meta.value: DOE-25 Salaries-Benefits sheet, accounts 1100 to 1400 (regular, special, vocational and other instructional programs), general and special revenue funds, FY2018 to FY2025.

meta.label: Student growth and student groups
meta.value: NH DOE disaggregated assessment files: mean student growth percentile (SGP) for reading and math; reading proficiency for students with IEPs and economically disadvantaged students. Subgroup cohorts are small and swing from year to year.

meta.label: Local school tax rates
meta.value: NH DOE, Valuations, Property Tax Assessments and Tax Rates of School Districts, tax years 2017 to 2025 (rows for Durham, Lee and Madbury); tax year 2026 from NH Department of Revenue Administration rates posted to date. Local education rate per $1,000 and total rate; tax year Y is shown against school year Y to Y+1. Tax years 2020 to 2025 agree with the DRA municipal rate sheets. Lee's 2026 rate was not yet set. Rates move with revaluations as well as spending.

meta.label: Property values and school levy by town
meta.value: Same NH DOE valuation files: equalized valuation with utilities and local education tax assessed for schools for Durham, Lee and Madbury, tax years 2017 to 2025. The three towns sum to the Oyster River Coop row in every year, and the levy equals DOE-25 local property tax revenue for FY2018 to FY2025. Shares of levy and value, value per student and levy per $1,000 are computed here.

meta.label: Per-student measures
meta.value: Special programs, plant operations, transportation, bond interest, local property tax and state aid from the DOE-25 District Profile divided by October 1 enrollment (NH DOE). Cost per pupil by school level is the NH DOE figure for elementary, middle and high school.

meta.label: State adequacy aid
meta.value: NH DOE Bureau of School Finance, Adequate Education Aid municipal summaries (ad_ed_aid and adequacy muni-summary files), SFY 2018 to 2027. Oyster River's figures are the sum of its three member towns, Durham, Lee and Madbury: total calculated cost of an adequate education, the Statewide Education Property Tax (SWEPT) the towns retain, and the final total state grant (adequacy grant plus SWEPT). For 2017-18 to 2024-25 the three-town grant total equals the adequacy aid reported in the district's DOE-25 to the dollar. 2025-26 and 2026-27 are the state's published estimates (April 2026 and the SFY 2027 file); the district has not filed those years.

meta.label: Cost per pupil comparison
meta.value: NH DOE Bureau of School Finance, Cost per Pupil by District, 2017-18 to 2024-25. State average is the DOE-published average for district-operated schools. Median and rank are computed here from the same file among the 52 to 54 districts that report elementary, middle and high school costs (K-12 districts). Districts with different grade ranges are not strictly comparable.

meta.label: Teacher pay and staffing
meta.value: NH DOE Bureau of Education Statistics: Teacher Minimum Starting Salary (bachelor's degree, no experience), Teacher Average Salary in Public School Districts (2017-18 to 2025-26) and Student to Teacher Ratio in New Hampshire Public Schools (2017-18 to 2021-22 from the static files; 2022-23 to 2025-26 from the iPlatform Student Teacher Ratio by District report, Oct 1 counts). 2025-26 average salary and teacher education (also 2019-20) come from the iPlatform Teacher Average Salary and Teacher Attainment reports. State figures are the DOE's own: unweighted average of districts for starting salary, state average salary and state total ratio. Oyster River's 2022-23 average salary ($63,538) and 2024-25 average salary ($80,573, identical to 2023-24) look unreliable in the DOE files and are not plotted.

meta.label: Enrollment
meta.value: October 1 fall enrollment, district total, NH DOE iExplore (Total Enrollment, entity Oyster River Coop (District)), 2016-17 to 2025-26; 2026-27 is the district's own October 7, 2026 count (the DOE has not published it). State-first rule: where the district's annual report prints a different figure the DOE figure is used. For 2018-19, 2019-20 and 2025-26 the report prints 2,157, 2,168 and 2,038, which equal the sum of the DOE's four school figures and the DOE student-to-teacher file; the DOE district total is 33, 34 and 26 higher. See CONFLICTS.md.

meta.label: Enrollment by school level
meta.value: October 1 counts for kindergarten to grade 4, grades 5 to 8 and grades 9 to 12 as printed in the ORCSD 2026 Annual Report (NH DOE history); they equal the DOE iExplore school figures (Mast Way + Moharimet, Middle, High) except grade 9-12 in 2025-26, where iExplore has 796 and the page uses it. From 2018-19 on the levels fall 25 to 34 students short of the DOE district total because some students are not itemized by level.

meta.label: General Fund balance
meta.value: NH DOE DOE-25 balance sheet (DOE25 sheet, rows 'Total Fund Equity' and the reserve and unassigned lines), Oyster River Coop workbooks for FY2018 to FY2025: the General Fund column at June 30, with the components the DOE-25 prints (reserved for prepaid expenses, reserved for amounts voted, reserved for encumbrances, unassigned fund balance retained, unassigned fund balance) and the trust-fund column (capital reserves) separately. The district's audited statements report a higher General Fund balance because they fold the trust funds in; the comparison is in CONFLICTS.md. FY2026 is not yet filed (the DOE posts ORCSD's report in mid to late December).

meta.label: Special education spending and offsetting revenue
meta.value: NH DOE DOE-25, FY2018 to FY2025: the detailed special education expenditure page (page 21: instruction, related services, administration, legal and transportation for handicapped and disabled students), special-program tuition from the tuition page (page 22), and the revenue accounts for state special education aid (3230), federal disabilities programs (4570) and Medicaid distributions (4580). The district's own table per RSA 32:11-a in its 2025 and 2026 annual reports matches these revenue lines, related services and transportation to the dollar but prints a different instruction figure; it is compared in CONFLICTS.md.

meta.label: General Fund spending by type
meta.value: NH DOE DOE-25 Annual Financial Report, DOE25 sheet (pages 7 to 10), Oyster River Coop workbooks for FY2018 to FY2025: the line \"Total Expenditures General Fund\" split into salaries, employee benefits, purchased services (accounts 300 to 500), supplies, property and other. Personnel is salaries plus benefits. The General Fund only; food service and grants are separate funds. FY2026 is not yet filed.

meta.label: Spending by school
meta.value: NH DOE DOE-25, School Level Expenditures sheet (required for federal civil-rights reporting), Oyster River Coop workbooks for FY2019 to FY2025: each school's state/local plus federal expenditures. Out-of-district tuition and transportation is shown on its own line from FY2024 (and is left out of the school total on the page); the FY2019 to FY2023 sheets do not break it out, so it is not stated whether those years' school lines include it. The preschool program has its own line from FY2022. Per-pupil figures divide by the October 1 enrollment in the NH DOE iExplore enrollment report. The sheet does not exist in the FY2018 workbook.

meta.label: Instructional pay by job class
meta.value: NH DOE DOE-25, Salaries-Benefits sheet, FY2018 to FY2025: salaries and benefits of teachers, aides and paraprofessionals, and other instructional staff, summed over regular programs (1100), special programs (1200), vocational (1300) and other instructional programs (1400). General and special revenue funds. Totals tie to the DOE-25 instruction salaries and benefits on the District Profile.

meta.label: Fund results by fund
meta.value: NH DOE DOE-25, Statement of Analysis of Change in Fund Equity (DOE25 sheet), FY2018 to FY2025: revenue and other additions less expenditures and other deletions, and fund equity at June 30, for the General Fund, the Food Service Fund and the Special Revenue Fund (federal and other grants). Each year's opening equity equals the prior year's closing equity to within a few cents, except where the district's own entries differ (see CONFLICTS.md).

meta.label: Long-term obligations
meta.value: Audited statements of the Oyster River Cooperative School District, statement of net position at June 30, fiscal years ended 2018 to 2024: bonds and loans payable (current and long-term portions), net pension liability (the district's share of the NH Retirement System) and net OPEB liability (retiree health), page 14 of each audit. The same statement gives total net position and the statement of activities gives interest expense. Accrual basis; the pension and OPEB figures are actuarial estimates as of the measurement dates the audits use.

meta.label: Pension and retiree health shares in the NH Retirement System
meta.value: NH Retirement System (NHRS) employer reporting schedules, GASB 68 (pension) and GASB 75 (retiree health), measurement dates June 30, 2017 to June 30, 2025, line 'Oyster River Coop SD' (the teacher group): proportionate share of the employer pool, net pension liability, deferred outflows and inflows, pension expense, employer contributions, and for the medical subsidy the share, net OPEB liability, expense and contributions. The district's audit uses NHRS's figures one year after the measurement date, so a June 30, 2023 measurement is shown under fiscal year 2024; this lets the page show FY2025 and FY2026 before those audits are posted. The audited net pension liability for FY2018 to FY2024 equals the NHRS figure exactly. The medical subsidy is only part of the district's total retiree health liability. The PDFs are mirrored in raw/nhrs/ and build/verify_nhrs.py re-reads every value from them.

meta.label: Budget versus actual spending by department
meta.value: General Fund Budget Comparison, 'Budget Summary by Location' in the ORCSD annual reports 2018 to 2024 (page 20 to 22): approved budget for the year and actual expenditure two years back, by department (Mast Way, Moharimet, Middle School, High School, Special Education, SAU/administration, Transportation, Technology, Facilities). General Fund (Fund 10) only; debt service and food service are outside the table. Approved includes warrant articles passed separately (contracts) where the table includes them. FY2024 approved rows add to $1,000 more than the printed total.

meta.label: Default budget and budget by fund
meta.value: Operating budget warrant article as printed in each annual report (2018 to 2026): the split by fund (Fund 10 general, 21 food service, 22 federal, 23 pass-through) and the default budget that applies if the article fails. Same totals as the adopted-budget row.

meta.label: Estimated tax-rate impact of the proposed budget
meta.value: 'Tax Rate Impacts & Apportionment' (2018 to 2024 reports) and 'Estimated Tax Impact' (2025, 2026 reports): the local school tax rate per $1,000 for the current budget year and as proposed, by town, with assessed value held fixed in both columns. The page shows proposed rate minus current rate. The printed 'impact' figure disagrees with that difference in some years (see CONFLICTS.md). The actual change is the later DOE/DRA rate minus the prior year's, which also reflects revaluations.

meta.label: Class size
meta.value: Average class size by grade band (grades 1 and 2, grades 3 and 4) for Mast Way and Moharimet schools and the NH average, as printed in the Annual Report Card in the ORCSD annual reports, 2017-18 to 2024-25; 2025-26 from the NH DOE iPlatform Average Class Size By School report (as of Oct 1, 2025). Middle school class size is not reported.

meta.label: SAT scores
meta.value: Oyster River High School and New Hampshire average SAT evidence-based reading and writing plus math (total out of 1600), spring 2018 to 2025. Oyster River High School comes from the ORCSD annual reports (counseling office); the New Hampshire average is the College Board's New Hampshire SAT annual report (Total row, all graduates who took the SAT), which the NH DOE hosts. The district's reports print different New Hampshire figures for 2019 to 2025 (listed in CONFLICTS.md); the state's are used. National averages in the report are not used because the printed 2019 values look inconsistent.

meta.label: Counselor ratio, certified teachers, students with disabilities
meta.value: NH DOE iExplore dashboard (dashboards.nh.gov, Tableau), entity 'Oyster River Coop (District)' and 'State of New Hampshire': students per school counselor (2020-21 on), share of classes taught by an educator certified in the subject, and students with disabilities as a share of enrollment, 2017-18 to 2025-26, school years as the DOE labels them.

meta.label: Suspension rates (share of students)
meta.value: NH DOE iReport (jwt.nh.gov, iReport/FrontPage, ESSA Profiles (District), entity Oyster River Coop): in-school and out-of-school suspension rates for All Students, 2017-18 to 2025-26, shown in the suspension tooltip; they also give 2025-26 before the DOE posts the school safety counts. Expulsion rate is 0.00 in every year.

meta.label: Four-year graduation rate
meta.value: NH DOE iExplore dashboard (dashboards.nh.gov, Tableau), entity 'Oyster River Coop (District)': four-year and five-year cohort graduation rates for 2017-18 to 2025-26 and post-secondary enrollment within a year (2017-18 to 2024-25). The DOE dashboard shows no New Hampshire comparison that is a graduation rate, so none is plotted.

meta.label: State test participation
meta.value: NH DOE iAchieve (assessment participation): share of students required to take the state English language arts, math and science assessments, 2017-18 to 2025-26. No test was given in spring 2020 (COVID-19). Federal accountability expects 95%.

meta.label: What graduates do next
meta.value: High School Completers table in the ORCSD annual reports: share of graduates entering four-year college, two-year college, work and military, district and NH, 2017-18 to 2023-24; 2024-25 from the NH DOE iPlatform report Completers By Status By School (preliminary, 218 Oyster River completers; 'work' = percent employed).

meta.label: Special education, lunch eligibility and English learners
meta.value: Special education counts as of October 1 from the district special education department, as printed in the ORCSD annual reports; free and reduced lunch eligibility and English learner counts from NH DOE as printed in the reports. Shares are computed here against October 1 enrollment.

meta.label: Education Freedom Account students
meta.value: NH DOE Education Freedom Account reports by municipality (June 2022, June 2023, April 2024, March 2025, March 2026): weighted counts of participating students living in Durham, Lee and Madbury and the aid awarded to them. The program began in 2021-22. These are residents, not necessarily former Oyster River students.

meta.label: Dropouts and career technology
meta.value: Dropout counts (district and NH) and Tri-City Career Technology Center enrollment of ORHS students, from the ORCSD annual reports, 2017-18 to 2024-25.

meta.label: Teacher education and experience
meta.value: Share of professional staff with a bachelor's, master's or higher degree (district and NH) and counts of staff with 14 or more years of experience by school, from the ORCSD annual reports (2017-18 to 2024-25). The 2019-20 education table is not printed.

meta.label: Attendance by school level
meta.value: Attendance by school level from the ORCSD annual reports, 2017-18 to 2022-23, district and NH. Later years are not plotted: the 2023-24 column repeats 2022-23 and 2024-25 looks re-based.

meta.label: Enrollment projections
meta.value: Projections of K-12 enrollment as printed in the ORCSD annual reports: the district's Long Range Planning Committee (2018 to 2024 editions, 2018-19 onward) and NESDEC (2021 to 2024 editions, 2021-22 onward). Each year shows the latest projection printed before that school year began; the 2024 edition repeats the 2023 tables and the 2025 and 2026 editions print none. Shown against actual October 1 enrollment (NH DOE).

meta.label: How the three towns share the school bill
meta.value: Formula: the NH DOE's Apportionment Formulas for Regional and Cooperative School Districts (July 1, 2024) says Oyster River apportions the total operating budget 50% on average daily membership (ADM) and 50% on equalized valuation, with adequacy aid credited to the pre-existing districts (the towns). Each town's formula share is printed in the ORCSD annual reports for FY2018 to FY2024 (the tax rate impact and apportionment page). For FY2025 and FY2026 it is the combined percentage on the NH DOE cooperative apportionment sheets published by the Department of Revenue Administration (2024 and 2025 Regional and Cooperative School District Apportionments; state credits are the final state aid on the same sheets); the FY2027 figure is an estimate from the latest DOE files (the sheet for the split approved Oct 30, 2026 is not posted yet). Students and property value behind each share: NH DOE Equalized Valuation per Pupil files (ADM in residence and equalized valuation with utilities, per town); the formula uses the latest file available when the budget is set, which lags the budget year by two to three years. A 50/50 average of those two shares reproduces the official percentage to within 0.01 point for FY2018 to FY2022 and FY2024. State credits are each town's adequacy grant plus the state education property tax (SWEPT) it keeps, from the annual reports (FY2018 to FY2023), the DOE adequate education aid municipal summaries (FY2024) and the DOE apportionment sheets (FY2025 and FY2026). State education tax rates per $1,000 are from the same annual report tables.

meta.label: Students living in each town
meta.value: NH DOE iPlatform, Town Level Enrollment By Grade (ReportID 12, my.doe.nh.gov/iPlatform): public-school students (preschool to grade 12) by town of residence as of October 1, Durham, Lee and Madbury, 2017-18 to 2026-27, with kindergarten to grade 4, grades 5 to 8 and grades 9 to 12 bands computed here. These are residents wherever they attend and differ from district enrollment, which includes tuition students. The 2026-27 counts are the DOE's first run (Oct 1, 2026) and may change.

meta.label: Results and staffing by school
meta.value: NH DOE iExplore Compare dashboard (jwt.nh.gov, iExplore/Explore-Dashboard) for Oyster River High School, Middle School, Mast Way and Moharimet, 2015-16 to 2025-26: students enrolled, share at levels 3 and 4 in reading and math, mean growth percentile (grades 4 to 8), students with disabilities, certified-teacher share, experienced-educator share, students per counselor and per non-teacher staff member, shown in the tooltips of the matching rows. High school proficiency is grade 11. District and state experienced-educator shares and students per non-teacher staff (2020-21 on) come from the same dashboard.

meta.label: State accountability ratings
meta.value: NH DOE iReport, ESSA Indicators (District), Oyster River schools, 2017-18 to 2025-26: ratings from 1 to 4 for achievement, growth, equity, college and career and graduation. None were issued for 2019-20; growth and equity were not rated in 2020-21. The plotted line averages the schools' ratings.

meta.label: Students with disabilities in regular classes
meta.value: NH DOE iReport, IDEA Report (district and State of New Hampshire), 2017-18 to 2024-25: share of students ages 6 to 21 with an IEP in regular classes 80% or more, under 40%, and in separate schools. 2018-19 is left blank because the DOE file repeats 2017-18 for both the district and the state.

meta.label: Staff by category
meta.value: NH DOE iPlatform, FTE Staff by District (ReportID 38), October 1, 2017-18 to 2025-26: teachers, instruction support, specialists, librarians, administrative support and all other support, in full-time equivalents. 'All other support' dropped from 73.7 to 41.5 in 2025-26 with no explanation in the report.

meta.label: State rates for suspension and truancy
meta.value: New Hampshire suspension rates: NH DOE iReport, entity State of New Hampshire (in-school and out-of-school, All Students). New Hampshire truancy: computed here as habitually truant students over enrollment from the DOE school safety workbooks (2017-18 to 2024-25) for all New Hampshire schools reporting.

meta.label: Assessment results
meta.value: NH DOE state assessment disaggregated files (2017-18 to 2025-26); District Level, All students, All grades, regular denominator; share at levels 3 and 4 in reading (ELA), math and science. No results exist for 2019-20.

meta.label: Revenue detail (DOE-25)
meta.value: DOE-25 revenue lines, FY2018 to FY2025: school meal revenue by source (Food Service Fund: meal sales, federal and state child nutrition, other), federal aid by program (special education IDEA, school lunch, Title I and other ESEA, Medicaid distributions, pandemic relief = ESSER plus other restricted federal aid through the state plus direct federal aid), General Fund other local revenue (earnings on investments, rentals, other), bond and note proceeds, and transfers from capital reserve and trust funds into the General Fund. Federal programs add to the DOE-25's federal total, which equals the federal revenue on the District Profile in every year (build/verify_doe25_more.py). FY2026 appears with the DOE-25 (mid-December).

meta.label: Tuition, transportation and bond schedule (DOE-25)
meta.value: Tuition paid to other schools by program (regular, special, vocational) and destination, student transportation by type of trip (accounts 2721 to 2729), and the district's bond debt schedule (remaining principal and interest at June 30 and the payments due in the next fiscal year, by issue), all from the DOE-25 workbooks, ACTIVITY table and the debt-schedule lines of the fund equity statement, FY2018 to FY2025. Special-program tuition covers students placed in other schools for special education and similar services. The DOE-25 function-code transportation total is 0.3% to 3.6% above the sum of the trip types, and the audited bonds-and-loans figure equals the DOE-25 schedule through FY2020 and is higher afterward; neither difference is reconciled in the filings. FY2026 appears with the DOE-25 (mid-December).

meta.label: Reading and math results by town of residence
meta.value: NH DOE 'by town responsible' assessment workbooks (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 tests), District Level, Oyster River Coop, All grades, All students: share at levels 3 and 4 in reading and math for students living in Durham, Lee and Madbury (the page averages the two subjects); science, growth and the tested count appear in the hover. Suppressed cells are left out. Extracted by build/town_results_extract.py to build/town_results.json; build/verify_town_results.py ties the town figures to the district's own results. The DOE publishes these files from the 2022 test on.

meta.label: Rank among NH towns on school tax rate
meta.value: NH DOE Bureau of School Finance, 'Valuations, Property Tax Assessments and Tax Rates of School Districts', tax years 2017 to 2025 (shown against the school year that follows): every town's equalized local education (school) tax rate per $1,000 of equalized valuation with utilities. Durham, Lee and Madbury are ranked among the roughly 230 to 242 towns with a nonzero rate (rank 1 = lowest; percentile 100 = highest). Extracted by build/town_rates_extract.py to build/town_rates.json; build/verify_town_rates.py compares the DOE school rate with the DRA's equalized school tax rate for every town, 2020 to 2024 (99% agree within 2 cents).

meta.label: ORCSD among New Hampshire K-12 districts
meta.value: Peer set: the districts that report elementary, middle and high cost per pupil in the NH DOE Bureau of School Finance cost per pupil file for the year (53 or 54 a year; FY2026 uses the FY2025 set because the FY2026 file is not out). Results: NH DOE statewide disaggregated assessment files, District Level, All grades, All students, regular denominator, share at levels 3 and 4 in reading (ELA) and math; the page averages the two. Growth: mean student growth percentile in reading and math, averaged. Low-income share: tested students in the SES (socioeconomically disadvantaged) subgroup over all tested students, from the DOE's rounded student counts (midpoints of the printed ranges). Ranks: 1 = highest. Percentile: 100 = highest of the districts. Expected proficiency: straight-line fit of proficiency on low-income share across the peer districts of the same year; the difference is the residual. A description of where ORCSD sits, not a measure of what any dollar or program produced. Built by build/peers.py from files in raw/nh-doe.
